newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended higher across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.70/98.75 compared with Tuesday's close of S$98.52/98.57, September 2001 at S$97.42/97.45 against S$97.20/97.25 and June 2003 at S$95.40/95.45 from S$95.13/95.18.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent versus Tuesday's 3 2-7/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.20/1.15 percent against Tuesday's yield of 1.28/1.23 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.75/1.70 percent from 1.85/1.80 percent.
